paper_title: AttentionInfluence Adopting Attention Head Influence for Weak-to-Strong   Pretraining Data Selection
caption: The statistics of clustering. The left is the clustering result of AttentionInfluence, the right part is that of FineWeb-Edu Classifier.
model_annotation: This pie chart visualizes the distribution of categories within the FineWeb-Edu Classifier clustering results. The chart comprises 21 slices, each representing a distinct category with a label. These categories include “Teaching & resources” (teal, approximately 17%), “Education” (yellow, approximately 38%), “Science & technology education” (cyan, approximately 19%), “History & Society” (orange, approximately 19%), “Health & Medicine” (pink, approximately 22%), “Diseases” (red, approximately 10-11%), “Nutrition” (purple, approximately 7%), “Animal & Plant” (dark red, approximately 12-13%), “Materials” (brown, approximately 2-3%), “Historical review” (light brown, approximately 7-12%), “Society & culture” (peach, approximately 10%), “Events & people” (gold, approximately 2-6%), “Infor tech” (beige, approximately 3-5%), “Materials” (brown, approximately 3%), “Emerging tech” (light blue, approximately 4%), "Fin & Engineer" (dark cyan, approximately 3%), “Tech & Engineer” (dark cyan, approximately 8-12%), “Policy” (blue, approximately 1%), “Manage” (grey, approximately 1-2%), and “Healthy education” (light cyan, approximately 2%). The chart appears to be arranged with segments generally ordered by decreasing proportion, though this is not strict. Percentage values are included directly within several of the slices. A legend is not present, but category labels are directly connected to their corresponding segments with lines.
